_comment: Labeled cases for scoring the interpreter across LLMs. One JSON object per line; lines starting with _comment are ignored. Fields: id, category, transcript, context (earlier lines, optional), voice (a ser.analyze() dict, or null for text-only), expect (acceptable tones -- a LIST because several readings are legitimately defensible), note (why this case exists). Scoring is 'is the model's tone in expect', so keep expect honest rather than narrow: a case where two tones are genuinely arguable should list both, or it punishes the model for being right.
--- literal / neutral: the guard rail. Over-reading tone into plain speech is the most damaging failure for this app, because it teaches a listener to distrust ordinary sentences.

transcript: The train leaves at four fifteen from platform two.
note: Pure information. Anything but neutral is over-reading.

transcript: I'll be in the office until about six today.
note: Plain logistics.

transcript: Can you send me the file when you get a chance?
note: Ordinary polite request. 'When you get a chance' is genuine softening, not passive aggression.

transcript: We tried that approach last quarter and it didn't work.
note: Negative content stated factually. Both readings defensible.

transcript: It's raining again.
note: Mild complaint or plain observation; no way to tell from text.

_comment: --- sarcasm evident from the words alone, no voice data. The classic case.

transcript: Oh great, another meeting that could have been an email.
note: Textbook. Failing this means failing the product's core promise.

transcript: Wow, you actually showed up on time today. Miracle.
note: Backhanded compliment; 'miracle' is the tell.

transcript: Sure, because that plan worked out so well last time.
note: 'so well last time' inverts the surface positive.

transcript: No, please, take your time. It's not like I have anywhere to be.
note: Explicit negation pattern.

_comment: --- passive aggression: hostility wearing agreeable words. The hardest category for a text-only model.

transcript: Fine. Whatever you think is best.
context: I still think we should go with the second option.
note: Context makes the capitulation visibly reluctant. Plain 'positive' is wrong.

transcript: It's fine, I'll just do it myself like always.
note: 'like always' is the grievance marker.

transcript: Thanks for finally getting back to me.
note: 'finally' turns thanks into a complaint.

transcript: Must be nice to have time for lunch breaks.
note: Envy/resentment dressed as an observation.

_comment: --- genuinely positive: the other guard rail. A model biased toward suspicion is as useless as one that misses sarcasm.

transcript: That's a really clever solution, I wouldn't have thought of that.
note: Sincere praise with no inversion markers.

transcript: Thanks so much for your help today, it made a real difference.
note: Specific gratitude reads as genuine.

transcript: I'm really looking forward to seeing everyone on Saturday.
note: Plain enthusiasm.

_comment: --- polite refusal: soft words, real 'no'. The read matters more than the tone label here.

transcript: I'd love to, but I've got a lot on my plate right now.
context: Any chance you could take this on as well?
note: A no. 'positive' would mislead the listener into expecting a yes.

transcript: Let me think about it and get back to you.
context: So can you commit to the deadline?
note: Non-commitment; often a soft no.

_comment: --- VOICE MISMATCH: the reason ser.py exists. These pairs hold the TEXT constant and vary only the voice, so a model that ignores the voice field scores identically on both halves and is exposed. This is the most important block in the file.

transcript: Oh wonderful. That is just perfect.
note: Positive words + genuinely bright voice = take literally. Pairs with mm-01b.

transcript: Oh wonderful. That is just perfect.
note: Identical words, hostile voice = sarcasm. Pairs with mm-01a.

transcript: I'm so happy for you.
note: Congratulation that is what it appears to be.

transcript: I'm so happy for you.
note: Warm words, flat sad voice: masking. Should NOT read as plain positive.

transcript: You are unbelievable, you know that?
note: Harsh-looking words + bright voice = teasing/banter, not a complaint.

transcript: You are unbelievable, you know that?
note: Same words, angry voice = a real complaint.

transcript: It's fine.
context: Are you sure you don't mind?
note: Calm even voice: actually fine.

transcript: It's fine.
context: Are you sure you don't mind?
note: The canonical 'it's fine' that is not fine.

_comment: --- low-confidence voice: the model must NOT let a weak acoustic guess override plain words. Tests the SER_MIN_CONFIDENCE instruction in the system prompt.

transcript: The meeting is moved to Thursday at ten.
note: Weak 'angry' guess on plain logistics. Must stay neutral -- this is the false-positive trap.

transcript: I finished the report and sent it over.
note: Weak 'sad' guess on a status update. Must stay neutral.

_comment: --- voice AGREES with words: no mismatch to resolve, so the read should be confident and literal.

transcript: I am so done with this whole situation.
note: Words and voice both negative. Should be an easy, confident negative.

transcript: This is the best news I've had all week.
note: Words and voice both positive.
